title: "Battle for Paradise: Puerto Rico, restrictions apply*" Exhibit
description: View a photo essay by Artist in Residence, Jo Cosme, that examines the tension between Puerto Rico as a marketed paradise and Puerto Rico as a lived reality.

customFields.label: Detailed Description
customFields.value:
"Battle for Paradise: Puerto Rico, restrictions apply*" is a photo essay by Jo Cosme that examines the tension between Puerto Rico as a marketed paradise and Puerto Rico as a lived reality.

Part of the ongoing project "Welcome to Paradise: ¡Viva Puerto Rico Libre!", the work focuses on how tourism, settler colonialism, and disaster-driven policies reshape who can remain on the archipelago and under what conditions.

Through photography and video, Cosme highlights the contrast between images designed to attract and the realities often kept out of frame - restricted access to land and beaches to the native population, rising costs of living, and the displacement of local communities. The phrase “restrictions apply” points to the fine print behind the promise of paradise, where access is uneven and shaped by power.

Rather than presenting Puerto Rico as a distant place, the work asks viewers to consider their proximity to these systems and what it means to move through them, whether as tourists, settlers, investors, or witnesses.

Thanks to our sponsor The Seattle Public Library Foundation.

Free and reduced access supported by 4Culture.

At storytime, kids ages 0-5 and their families can enjoy stories, songs, and fun learning activities.

Early Learning is a great way for kids ages 0-5 and their families to develop learning, literacy, and language skills as well as community with other families.

We read stories, sing songs, and have engaging, educational activities that help kids and their caregivers grow together.

title: Adult Tutoring
description: Meet with a volunteer tutor one-on-one or in a small group for help with basic skills for English, writing, math, citizenship interview and exam, and high school completion.

eventImage.alt: Two images. On the left side, two adults sitting and talking at a table. On the right side, exterior of library location.

customFields.label: Detailed Description
customFields.value:
Visit anytime between 10:30 am - 12:30 pm on Saturdays to practice with a volunteer tutor.
  • Learn basic skills: English language (including ESOL), reading, writing, and math.
  • Work towards educational goals: high school diploma, GED, college application essay and placement tests, and college degree.
  • Prepare for US citizenship: interview and 100 civics questions.
Thanks to our sponsor The Seattle Public Library Foundation.

customFields.label: Event Logistics
customFields.value:
Books & materials provided.

This is a drop-in program (pre-registration is not required) but space is limited by the number of tutors available.

Learners will be assigned a tutor on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of tutoring sessions may be limited to serve as many learners as possible.
